title: Complementary module restrictions in independent coefficient universes
statement: Let X and Z be schemes in universe t [def-pc-scheme], i:Z -> X a closed immersion and U an object of the small pro-etale site of X whose structure map is a quasi-compact open immersion with image the complement of i(Z) [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Set v=max(u,t+1), let R be any commutative ring sheaf with sections in v, and let A be its underlying ring sheaf. On v-sized A-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], let L and J be the actual localized extension and slice restriction [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. Let I be the forgetful functor to abelian sheaves followed by the constructed abelian inverse image along i [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Then I(L(M)) is zero for every module sheaf M on the slice. Moreover, for every A-linear morphism f, if J(f) and I(f) are isomorphisms, f is an isomorphism. No assertion that L preserves products is assumed or concluded, and neither X nor Z is required to be quasi-compact or separated.

proof.text: Forget the actual module extension to the abelian sheafification of its direct-sum presheaf P, using the definition of module sheafification. For any abelian sheaf H on Z, all maps P -> i_*H are zero: on a summand indexed by a map V -> U, disjointness makes V times_X Z empty and the empty-cover sheaf axiom makes H on this object zero. Direct-sum induction proves equality of any two presheaf maps, including the empty-index case. The inverse-image and sheafification Hom adjunctions then make I(L(M)) initial, hence zero in the category of abelian sheaves.

To detect isomorphisms, cover each test object by its affine opens and refine them by bounded faithfully flat weakly etale affine extensions with the ring-retraction property. On a resulting Spec B the complementary open is compact, so choose finitely many elements defining its closed complement set-theoretically. The basic opens of these elements and the localization at elements invertible modulo their ideal form a pro-etale cover. Basic opens map to U. The closed-localization ring retains the ring-retraction property, and each of its points specializes to the closed fibre. Compose these covers, keeping every scheme in t.

Evaluation on the closed-localization piece carries every epimorphism of Type(max u (t+1))-valued sheaves to a surjection, by the ring-retraction evaluation theorem, which already permits an independent section universe. Apply the independent-universe abelian specialization theorem to the actual constructed abelian inverse-image adjunction. The closed units of the underlying abelian sheaves of M and N are bijective on this piece. Their naturality square and the assumed isomorphism I(f) show that f is bijective on its sections.

On each piece with a map to U, evaluate the isomorphism given by the actual localizedSystemRestriction(f) at the corresponding slice object. Its section map is exactly f on that piece. On all covering pieces f is therefore bijective. The image and equalizer sieves contain the generated covering sieves, so the underlying abelian sheaf map is locally surjective and locally injective. Mathlib Sheaf.isLocallyBijective_iff_isIso makes it invertible, and SheafOfModules.toSheaf reflects isomorphisms. This also treats empty pieces and zero coefficients.

lean.statement:
theorem proEtaleOpenClosedModuleSupportOfUniverses
    {X Z : Scheme.{t}} (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    (U : X.ProEt) [IsOpenImmersion U.hom] [QuasiCompact U.hom]
    (hU : Set.range U.hom = (Set.range i)ᶜ)
    (R : Sheaf (ProEt.topology X) CommRingCat.{max u (t + 1)}) :
    let A := (sheafCompose (ProEt.topology X)
      (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max u (t + 1)} RingCat.{max u (t + 1)})).obj R
    let I := SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{max u (t + 1)} A ⋙
      Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback (proEtaleBaseChange i)
        AddCommGrpCat.{max u (t + 1)} (ProEt.topology X) (ProEt.topology Z)
    (∀ M, IsZero (I.obj ((SheafOfModules.localizedSystemExtension.{t + 1, t, u}
      R U).obj M))) ∧
    (∀ {M N : SheafOfModules.{max u (t + 1)} A} (f : M ⟶ N),
      IsIso ((SheafOfModules.localizedSystemRestriction.{t + 1, t, u} R U).map f) →
      IsIso (I.map f) → IsIso f)
